item.title: Bitcoin verstehen – Episode 329 - Bitcoins unsichtbare Risiken und die Geduld, die du langfristig brauchst
item.description:
In dieser Folge sprechen wir über Morgan Housels Buch "Same As Ever" und was sich davon auf Bitcoin übertragen lässt. Wir gehen der These nach, dass das größte Risiko nie das ist, worüber alle reden, sondern das, was niemand kommen sieht. Außerdem schauen wir uns an, warum langfristiges Denken bei Bitcoin sich anfühlt wie eine Bergbesteigung in vielen kleinen, anstrengenden Schritten, und warum die meisten Bitcoin-Nachrichten schon nach einer Woche keine Rolle mehr spielen. Eine Folge über Geduld, Risiko und die Frage, wie viel Aufmerksamkeit wir dem Tagesgeschehen wirklich schenken sollten.


Du benötigst persönliche Unterstützung bei den Themen Aufbewahrung, Steuern & Vererbung von Bitcoin? Wir gestalten derzeit konkrete Inhalte, mit denen wir dir Schritt für Schritt helfen möchten. Trage dich jetzt in unsere Warteliste ein und werde als Erstes benachrichtigt, sobald es losgeht. Jetzt in die Warteliste eintragen.

Jeden Montag 5 interessante Medien rund um Bitcoin & Geld sowie donnerstags die Zusammenfassung unserer aktuellen Episode in euer Postfach? Dann melde dich zu unserem Newsletter an.

item.title: Dein Weg zu Bitcoin – Wie man mit Wörtern zaubert und Warum man die Geldgans nie schlachten darf – Nadin Hartmann erklärt Kindern Verkaufen und Finanzen – Dein Weg zu Bitcoin
item.description:
Nadin Hartmann, Gesundheitspädagogin, Mutter von zwei Kindern und Autorin des Kinderbuchs „Ein Papagei namens Selly“, das am 19. August erscheint. Wir sprechen darüber, wie man Kindern schwierige Themen wie Verkaufen, Geld und Gefühle kindgerecht beibringt, wie die „Geldgans“ ihren Kindern Sparen und Zinseszins erklärt – und wie Nadin als gelernte Gesundheits- und Krankenpflegerin irgendwann anfing, das etablierte Gesundheitssystem selbst zu hinterfragen.Ein Gespräch über Kinderbücher, die Geldgans, die Warnblinkleuchte deines Körpers – und eine überraschende Parallele zwischen Nährstoffverlust und Kaufkraftverlust, die Finanzen und Gesundheit für immer miteinander verbindet.

🧠 Themen in der Episode:• Warum es kaum Kinderbücher zu Themen wie Verkaufen, Geld oder Bitcoin gibt – und wie „Ein Papagei namens Selly“ das ändert• Wie Nadin ihren Kindern mit der „Geldgans“ Sparen, Investieren und Zinseszins beibringt• Warum „wohlhabend“ das bessere Wort ist als „reich“ oder „erfolgreich“• Wie Nadin zu Bitcoin fand – vom kompletten Unwissen zum Verständnis fürs Energie-Argument• Ihr Weg von der Skepsis („der will mir nur was verkaufen“) zur ganzheitlichen Gesundheitspädagogin• Warum Symptome behandeln nicht reicht – die Warnblinkleuchten- und die 47-Bausteine-Analogie• Die überraschende Parallele zwischen Nährstoffverlust in Lebensmitteln und Kaufkraftverlust durch Inflation• Warum Finanzen und Gesundheit für Nadin untrennbar zusammengehören (Lebensrad)

💬 Zitat der Folge:„Die Geldgans wird nie geschlachtet.“📲 Nadin findet ihr:• Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/diegesundheitspaedagogin/• Buch „Ein Papagei namens Selly“ (ab 19.08., jetzt vorbestellbar): https://amzn.eu/d/08EpLCcw ✨ Mein Ziel: Bitcoin verständlich und greifbar machen durch Geschichten, die jeder nachvollziehen kann und die zeigen, dass die ersten Schritte nicht groß sein müssen und dass jeder Zweifel am Anfang hatte. item.title: Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock'n'Roll – Tether, Revolut Stablecoin, and the Custody Wars | Monthly Briefing
item.description:
August delivered few headlines, but the markets refused to take a summer break. In this BFRR Monthly Briefing, co-hosts Dr. Jonas Gross and Manuel Klein examine Bitcoin’s sharp rise from roughly $63,000 to nearly $79,000, renewed inflows into spot ETFs and the macroeconomic signal sent by the U.S. Treasury’s decision to expand buybacks of longer-dated bonds. They also assess President Trump’s latest meeting with crypto executives and ask what another delay to the CLARITY Act means for the United States—and whether Europe can turn regulatory stability into an advantage.

The episode’s central question is more fundamental: Who should be trusted to safeguard digital assets? The COLDCARD incident, in which attackers exploited weak randomness in wallet seed generation and stole more than $100 million in Bitcoin, challenges the assumption that hardware wallets eliminate counterparty risk. Jonas and Manuel compare self-custody with institutional custody and explain why “don’t trust, verify” still depends on software, audits, operational discipline and human judgment. Citi’s forthcoming Bitcoin custody service provides the institutional counterpoint, combining digital assets with its broader Custody+ infrastructure.

The discussion then turns to private forms of digital money. Tether has completed its first full audit of its financial statements, receiving an unqualified opinion from KPMG U.S. Revolut is bringing euros on-chain with EURR, a new stablecoin issued by Stripe-owned Bridge, while Circle has named major financial institutions as founding validators for its Arc network. Standard Chartered and HSBC, meanwhile, have completed the first live cross-border tokenized-deposit transaction on Swift’s blockchain-based ledger.

In the Knowledge Bites, the hosts review a BaFin survey exposing persistent gaps in German investors’ understanding of crypto assets and a BlackRock paper on Bitcoin’s possible role in a traditional 60/40 portfolio. A concise look at the choices now shaping crypto custody, stablecoins and the future architecture of money.

Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock’n’Roll Website Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock’n’Roll Telegram Channel

Knowledge Bite Jonas: Re-Underwriting Bitcoin: Still a Portfolio Diversifier Knowledge Bite Manuel: Wissenslücken bei Krypto-Anlegerinnen und -Anlegern

item.title: Rob Wallace | Bitcoin News – "Bitcoin Has Waited 16 Years For This EXACT Moment" | Tom Luongo & Vince Lanci
item.description:
Bitcoin waited sixteen years for this exact moment. And according to Tom Luongo and Vince Lanci, it just became obvious.

Two friends who spend their lives tracking money, gold, and geopolitics take you on a tour around the entire global risk board. By the end of it, a failed trade deal with Canada, ninety billion barrels of Venezuelan oil, the CIA director landing in Moscow, and seized Iranian tankers sitting in a Texas court all connect into a single argument about who controls the long end of the American yield curve, and why Bitcoin's training wheels just came off.

Here is what we cover:

• Why Carney blew up the US-Canada trade deal and the real reason behind the obnoxious rhetoric on both sides

• Why the real split is not Canada from China, it is Canada from Europe and the City of London

• The ninety billion barrels of sour Venezuelan oil and why that news broke three days after the Canada trade talks collapsed

• Why CIA Director Ratcliffe flying to Moscow was a direct message to Europe

• Storm Shadow missiles and the terrifying question of whose finger is actually on the button

• Operation Economic Outcast and the full picture of how Iran is being sanctioned right now

• The seized Iranian tankers sitting in a Texas court and the collateral question nobody is asking

• What Bessent actually did with the bond buybacks and why almost everyone calling it yield curve control has it wrong

• Treasury QE explained and why banks are being used to finance the government in a completely new way

• The ten to fifteen year plan Vince and Tom believe is already underway to fix the US fiscal deficit

• Why macro funds are buying gold again and what that signals about where smart money sees this going

• Why Vince, a lifelong gold trader, believes Bitcoin's training wheels just came off and why it might be about to become the new gold

• The DARPA argument and why big Bitcoin might be closer to a national security asset than people realize

Everything about Bitcoin's story before this felt almost irrelevant. This conversation argues the big story has been staring us in the face the entire time.

🔔 Subscribe for weekly Bitcoin and macro analysis.

TIMESTAMPS

00:00 - Cold Open — Bitcoin's Training Wheels Just Came Off

01:33 - Carney Blows Up The US-Canada Trade Deal

06:53 - Splitting Canada From Europe And The City Of London Not China

15:27 - Venezuela Oil Reserves — 90 Billion Barrels Of Sour Crude

20:02 - CIA Director Ratcliffe Flies To Moscow — A Message To Europe

24:17 - Storm Shadow Missiles And Whose Finger Is On The Button

32:18 - Operation Economic Outcast — Sanctioning Iran Explained

36:20 - Seized Iranian Tankers In A Texas Court — Whose Collateral Is It

38:00 - What Bessent Actually Did With Treasury Bond Buybacks

45:47 - Why This Is Not Yield Curve Control

54:03 - Treasury QE Explained — How Banks Are Financing The Government

01:00:59 - The 10 To 15 Year Plan To Fix The US Fiscal Deficit

01:07:13 - Why Macro Funds Are Buying Gold Again

01:11:45 - Bitcoin's Training Wheels Come Off — Is It Becoming The New Gold?

item.title: The Bitcoin Frontier – Inside Wall Street’s bitcoin playbook with Denny Galindo
item.description:
Denny is a wealth manager and bitcoin research lead at Morgan Stanley, where he bridges traditional finance and bitcoin for high-net-worth investors. He operates inside one of the world’s largest financial institutions while developing frameworks to help advisors understand and allocate to bitcoin.

In this episode, Denny joins The Bitcoin Frontier to share how investors should think about bitcoin in a portfolio, the three core investor buckets driving adoption, and his thoughts on determining whether you’re underweight or overweight bitcoin. We dig into bitcoin’s market cycles and seasonal framework, the role of global money supply in driving returns, and practical strategies for gaining exposure in a volatile asset.

item.title: Swan Signal Live - A Bitcoin Show – John Haar Returns: Why the Fed Must Talk Tough While It Inflates
item.description:
• John reads Warsh's Jackson Hole speech as a nothing burger for Bitcoiners: a Fed chair must talk tough on inflation because signaling anything else would send inflation expectations and yields higher, while the long-run path of financial repression stays the same
  • Warsh reported that 54% of PCE basket components rose more than 3% over the past year, called 4.1% unemployment full employment, and framed inflation as squarely the Fed's problem to solve
  • Markets read the speech as hawkish anyway: the two-year yield rose about 12 basis points while gold and Bitcoin each gave back roughly 3.5%
  • On last week's expanded Treasury buybacks, John points to two signals: a 30-year yield near 5.3% is clearly bothering policymakers, and the Fed has never meaningfully reduced its holdings of 10-year-plus Treasuries even during quantitative tightening, evidence that natural buyers of long-dated government paper are scarce
  • The hosts revisit the shallowest bear market thesis they developed together on this show: a roughly 52% drawdown against 77% to 90%-plus in prior cycles, with the June low of $58,000 sitting just below the 200-week moving average before price rocketed back through it
  • John explains why he believes the June low will hold, while framing the 50-week moving average near $82,000 as the level the market is watching to declare a new bull market
  • Glassnode data shows 1.05 million Bitcoin of long-term holder supply with a cost basis between $83,000 and $86,000, the first heavy resistance shelf above spot, and the hosts discuss how cost basis shapes market psychology
  • The debasement trade is back in ETF volumes, with GLD and IBIT both in the top ten most traded funds, and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio breaking its year-long downtrend after gold's 2025 outperformance
  • Bitcoin's long correlation with software stocks broke down in June, and John argues it was always the wrong frame, a point Lyn Alden's Wall Street Journal essay makes at length: Bitcoin is a protocol of value, not another technology stock
  • A broad Treasury ETF has returned roughly negative 18% after inflation over fifteen years while the supply of government debt keeps expanding, the picture John says is quietly ending the era of Treasuries as the world's default store of value

item.title: The Bitcoin Matrix – Aaron Siri: The One Product You Can't Sue in America
item.description:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

Subscribe so you never miss an episode.

item.title: Bitcoin Audible – Learning the Wrong Lessons
item.description:
Thousands of careful Bitcoiners just got wiped out by a Coldcard entropy bug, and I use this episode to push back hard on the idea that self-custody is dead, and "don't trust, verify" failed us.

I walk through the brutal history of centralized custodial failures, explain why "holding your own keys is still orders of magnitude safer, and extract three real lessons from this recent disaster. This is about keeping perspective, learning the right lessons from pain, and making Bitcoin self-custody stronger, not weaker.

Chapters

(00:00:00) - Intro

(00:00:41) - Is self custody pointless

(00:03:07) - Only tradeoffs exist

(00:05:16) - History of exchange hacks

(00:08:27) - Custodial total losses

(00:08:27) - Not your keys

(00:09:35) - Coldcard loss in context

(00:10:55) - Bitcoin as antifragile

(00:11:46) - Open vs source available

(00:12:39) - Audits and entropy

item.title: The Mustard Seed Bitcoin Podcast – Bitcoin’s Power Law Has Held for 10 Years. What Comes Next? | Sminston With
item.description:
Sminston With joins me to explain why Bitcoin’s power law has remained remarkably consistent and how PMI, liquidity, and AI may help explain Bitcoin’s current cycle. We also discuss what could invalidate the power law, the possibility of a $200K-$300K Bitcoin supercycle, and why accumulating 1 BTC is becoming increasingly difficult.

item.title: TFTC: A Bitcoin Podcast – Ten31 Timestamp: Druck and Disorderly
item.description:
The Treasury declared economic D-Day on Iran the same week traffic through the Strait of Hormuz jumped 400% and Trump announced a deal for 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil. None of that is a coincidence.

🔗 https://bitcoinproducts.com

In this episode:

  • What Operation Economic Outcast and secondary sanctions are actually targeting
  • Why Bessent refused to rule out sanctioning Chinese banks
  • Reports of a canal being dredged in Oman to route around Hormuz
  • How the Venezuela deal more than doubles US access to proven reserves
  • Why Druckenmiller's op ed makes an argument that missed its exit 20 years ago
  • Trade unions turning into the loudest defenders of the AI build out

TIMESTAMPS:

00:00:00 - Jackson Hole in the rearview and a dressed down August recap

00:00:37 - Treasury's economic D-Day and Operation Economic Outcast

00:02:20 - Secondary sanctions covering digital assets, gold and shipping

00:02:47 - Whether Chinese banks are above the reach of US sanctions

00:24:55 - Print the difference or redesign the game board

item.title: Bitcoin Audible.DE - Die besten Bitcoin-Artikel, vorgelesen in deutscher Sprache! – 208. Martin Connor - Bitcoin, das ultimative Kollateral
item.description:
von Martin Connor – Originaltitel: «Bitcoin: The Ultimate Collateral«

*„Die beste, einfachste – ultimative – Form der Kreditsicherheit ist etwas, das sofort beansprucht und verkauft werden kann, wenn der Schuldner seine Zahlungen nicht leistet. Der Verkauf eines Hauses kann Monate oder sogar Jahre dauern. Auch Aktien haben zeitliche Beschränkungen. Bitcoin jedoch nicht. Bitcoin ist immer in Bewegung“
*

(Martin Connor)

Wenn man Bitcoin als hartes, in seinem Kern nicht veränderbares oder manipulierbares Asset begreift, welche Möglichkeiten eröffnen sich dadurch? Das Buch „Bitcoin: Die ultimative Kreditsicherheit“ untersucht, wie die Bereiche Bitcoin und Kreditvergabe perfekt zusammenpassen. Etwa, wie Bitcoin-Besitzer und Bitcoin-Unternehmen den maximalen Wert aus ihren Bitcoins herausholen können, ohne sie verkaufen zu müssen.

Wir lesen ein Kapitel aus diesem Buch, das eine zentrale Idee beleuchtet: Bitcoin als die beste Sicherheit, die die Menschheit je hatte. Die meisten Menschen denken beim Thema «Sicherheit» an Häuser, Aktien, Gold und Bargeld – aber weil es scheinbar nichts Besseres gab, übersehen sie deren enorme Schwächen. Die Kombination der Elemente von Multisignatur – echtes gemeinsames Eigentum, perfekte digitale Knappheit, Portabilität und die unübertroffene Verfügbarkeit von Bitcoin – unterscheidet es grundlegend von herkömmlichen Besicherungsmodellen.

Verkaufe Deine Bitcoins niemals – lebe davon.

Weitere Empfehlungen:

  • Pierre Rochard: «Der Nutzen des Sparens» (Ep. #019)
  • Tomer Strolight: «Warum Bitcoin?» (Ep. #80-82)
  • Saifedean Ammous: «Für eine Rückkehr zu niedriger Zeitpräferenz» (Ep. #77)
  • Pierre Rochard: «Bitcoin vs. Gold» (Ep. #71)
  • Hans-Hermann Hoppe: «Der Ertrag aus gespartem Geld – neu überdacht» (Ep. #18)
  • Parker Lewis: «Die «Bezahl‘ mich in Bitcoin!»-Theorie» (#140)
  • Parker Lewis: «Bitcoin-Zahlungen: Die ‹Jemand ist der Nächste›-Logik» (#151)
  • HodlHodl.com für Belehnung von Bitcoin, ebenso wie Unchained Capital, Ledn, Firefish etc.

Abonniere BitcoinAudible.de und empfehle unsere Vorlesungen jedem, der/die sich für Bitcoin interessiert. Hilf damit auch anderen, Bitcoin von einem starken monetären, wirtschaftlichen und philosophischen Fundament aus zu erkunden.

Unterstütze bitte unser Projekt und sende uns Sats via Lightning oder nütze eine der anderen Optionen.

Tipp: Bitcoin nur mehr KYC-frei kaufen! Auf HodlHodl.com ist das recht einfach, und mit Anmeldung über den obigen Link reduziert Du darüber hinaus sogar auch die Spesen für Deine ersten Käufe dort.

]]>

item.title: The Bitcoin Layer – Bitcoin Just Failed Three Times
item.description: <![CDATA[In this video, Nik covers the market reaction to Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, starting with the two-year yield pushing back toward its highs near 4.35% and what that says about the market pricing in rate hikes. He explains why the yield curve flattening from 50 to 37 basis points on the week is the move he finds most important, how a flattening curve prices growth out of the economy, and why Michael Howell's read frames it as a premium for safe assets. Nik also revisits the recession call TBL got wrong in 2022, and covers bitcoin's three failed attempts at $81,000 this week.]]>

item.title: Once Bitten! A Bitcoin Podcast. – Stolen Science Series Part 8 - VAERS - Dr Jessica Rose.
item.description:
VAERS stands for the 'Vaccine Adverse Effects Reporting System.'

$ BTC 63,961

Block Height 961,091

Today's guest is Dr. Jessica Rose, PhD, MSc, BSc.

Jessica is a Senior Fellow specializing in Computational Biology from Canada. She holds a Bachelor’s Degree in applied mathematics and a master’s degree in Immunology from Memorial University of Newfoundland, and a PhD in Computational Biology from Bar Ilan University.

Dr. Rose has completed two post-doctoral degrees in Molecular Biology from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and in Biochemistry from the Technion Institute of Technology. She is best known for her contributions to public health and safety related to the COVID-19 injectable products, and her analyses of pharmacovigilance databases like VAERS.

She joined me to discuss her analysis of the VAERS database and her critiques of the COVID-19 vaccine rollout and broader public health narratives.

Key Topics:

  • Analysis of the Vaccine Adverse Effects Reporting System (VAERS)
  • Criticisms of COVID-19 mRNA injection data and safety
  • Mechanisms of autoimmunity and potential side effects
  • Data censorship and manipulation in scientific literature

item.title: Bitcoiners - Live From Bitcoin Beach – These Salvadoran Brothers Are Building What Bitcoin Country Looks Like in 2030 | Diego Villeda & Mauricio Villeda of The Bitcoin Life
item.description:
Would you trust two brothers with zero aviation experience to run El Salvador's helicopter tours, plane charters, and Bitcoin travel experiences? Thousands of Bitcoiners already have. Today on Live From Bitcoin Beach, I sit down with Mauricio and Diego Villeda, founders of Bitcoin Life, the Bitcoin tourism and concierge service company that convinced El Salvador's Minister of Defense to lend them Air Force helicopters. I wanted the full story of how two guys orange-pilled by a $5K Bitcoin client built the most Bitcoin-native travel operation on the planet, and they didn't hold back.

It all started with a free Notion page built to help Bitcoiners travel El Salvador, covering transportation, places to stay, and spots that accept Bitcoin over the Lightning Network. Three days after launch, Stacy Herbert retweeted it, and strangers at the Adopting Bitcoin conference were showing the brothers their own guide without knowing who made it. That one retweet turned a side project into a company, and it proved something maxis have said for years, that proof of work beats marketing budgets.

These days the brothers run helicopter tours to places most tourists never see, including Lake Ilopango, a lake that had zero tourism when gangs controlled the area. They fly clients beyond El Zonte, land in soccer fields, and pay the local caretakers in sats to clear the space. For Bitcoiners flying in from abroad, they also run VIP airport pickups that take you from immigration straight to a helicopter, plane charters connecting El Salvador with Próspera in Honduras for around $3,000 per group, and real estate guidance for investors front-running the nation-state adoption wave. Every booking, vendor, and ticket runs on Bitcoin, feeding the Bitcoin circular economy that fiat skeptics love to claim doesn't exist.

Their biggest project is still ahead, a Bitcoin Street in the Centro Histórico of San Salvador where every business accepts Bitcoin, complete with an academy, an art gallery, and rooftop coffee shops. The brothers are raising from investors before Bitcoin Histórico this November, and I love their case for it. A district that was too dangerous to visit a few years ago deserves a permanent Bitcoin landmark, and low time preference built this country's turnaround.

If you've ever wanted to see El Salvador from a military helicopter while paying in sats, these are your guys. Subscribe for more stories from the ground, share this with your favorite nocoiner, and drop a comment telling me which tour you'd book first.


—Bitcoin Beach Team

Today on Live From Bitcoin Beach, I sit down with Mauricio and Diego Villeda, founders of Bitcoin Life, the Bitcoin tourism and concierge service company that convinced El Salvador's Minister of Defense to lend them Air Force helicopters. I wanted the full story of how two guys orange-pilled by a $5K Bitcoin client built the most Bitcoin-native travel operation on the planet, and they didn't hold back.

It all started with a free Notion page built to help Bitcoiners travel El Salvador, covering transportation, places to stay, and spots that accept Bitcoin over the Lightning Network. Three days after launch, Stacy Herbert retweeted it, and strangers at the Adopting Bitcoin conference were showing the brothers their own guide without knowing who made it. That one retweet turned a side project into a company, and it proved something maxis have said for years, that proof of work beats marketing budgets.

These days the brothers run helicopter tours to places most tourists never see, including Lake Ilopango, a lake that had zero tourism when gangs controlled the area. They fly clients beyond El Zonte, land in soccer fields, and pay the local caretakers in sats to clear the space. For Bitcoiners flying in from abroad, they also run VIP airport pickups that take you from immigration straight to a helicopter, plane charters connecting El Salvador with Próspera in Honduras for around $3,000 per group, and real estate guidance for investors front-running the nation-state adoption wave. Every booking, vendor, and ticket runs on Bitcoin, feeding the Bitcoin circular economy that fiat skeptics love to claim doesn't exist.

Their biggest project is still ahead, a Bitcoin Street in the Centro Histórico of San Salvador where every business accepts Bitcoin, complete with an academy, an art gallery, and rooftop coffee shops. The brothers are raising from investors before Bitcoin Histórico this November, and I love their case for it. A district that was too dangerous to visit a few years ago deserves a permanent Bitcoin landmark, and low time preference built this country's turnaround.

If you've ever wanted to see El Salvador from a military helicopter while paying in sats, these are your guys. Subscribe for more stories from the ground, share this with your favorite nocoiner, and drop a comment telling me which tour you'd book first.


—Bitcoin Beach Team

item.description:
The Last Trade: a $20 trillion carry trade sits underneath every market in the world, and when it unwinds, Bitcoin is what gets sold first. Jackson sits down with Roberto Rios, the macro analyst behind The Dollar Endgame, on Japan's $91 billion week defending the yen, the first time any major country has used the Fed's FEMA repo window to fund an intervention, and why Japan has roughly eight interventions left before the reserves run out.

---

👉 Get Back to Basics: 50% off trading fees + no-fee recurring buys — open your free account: https://go.onrampbitcoin.com/back-to-basics-tlt

The Last Trade: a weekly, bitcoin-native podcast covering the intersection of bitcoin, tech, & finance on a macro scale. Hosted by Jackson Mikalic, Michael Tanguma, & Brian Cubellis. Join us as we dive into what bitcoin means for how individuals & institutions save, invest, & propagate their purchasing power through time. It's not just another asset… in the digital age, it's The Last Trade that investors will ever need to make.


🎙️ About This Episode

Roberto Rios argues that Japan has been the world's creditor for thirty-five years, and that the bill for it is now coming due. He walks Jackson through the mechanics: three decades pinned at zero rates, a carry trade that lets traders borrow yen for free and buy anything yielding more, and a Bank of Japan that has spent roughly $320 billion since 2022 trying to stop the yen from dying. Deutsche Bank puts the carry trade at $20 trillion, and Rios puts its correlation to Bitcoin at 0.8, which is why every intervention has been followed by a Bitcoin drawdown within hours. Japan cannot raise rates out of the problem either: at 260% debt to GDP, every 100 basis points of average interest costs 23% of federal tax receipts, so a 4% average rate makes the government insolvent outright. The second half turns to the US, where Rios makes the case that the Treasury's bond buybacks are quantitative easing under another name, and traces the toolkit that has kept liquidity flowing with no easing program ever announced: the reverse repo drawdown, the BTFP, the December 2025 cut to the supplementary leverage ratio, and the reserve management purchase program. He closes on his bear market call, the $83,000 level he is watching, and a $200,000 target.


🧠 Chapters

00:00 - Introduction: Roberto Rios on Japan macro

01:53 - Japan as the world's creditor for thirty-five years

03:30 - Inside the $91 billion yen intervention

05:42 - Four years of failed interventions

07:22 - The FEMA repo window: a first for any major country

10:01 - The carry trade as a permanent bid under markets

11:53 - August 2024: the biggest Nikkei drop since 1987

13:10 - Bitcoin's 0.8 correlation to the yen carry trade

15:55 - Hawkish dissents and why the Fed is holding rates

18:47 - Japan's debt math: 260% of GDP and insolvency

20:37 - The monetary reset: defaulting to the Bank of Japan

25:10 - What the Treasury buyback program actually does

29:25 - Duration swaps and QE without calling it QE

33:54 - Reverse repo, the BTFP, the SLR cut, and the RMP

40:50 - Why liquidity keeps flowing into AI and data centers

43:58 - Save the bonds or save the currency, not both

46:39 - Yield curve control and QE infinity

57:39 - Bitcoin: the bear market call, $83K, and $200K


💡 Subscribe & Stay Ahead

BritishHODL dominated an hour of the show with some great points on Bitcoin insurance and Bitcoin lending - and why, when you really dig into both, they look weak at best. We broke down the assumptions, the risks, and whether either model actually makes sense in a Bitcoin-native world.

We then moved on to the new Blake Chain, digging into what’s happening there and what it could mean for the broader Bitcoin ecosystem - plus the usual mix of Bitcoin, markets, builders, and whatever else is making noise.

🗓️ Monday–Friday
⏰ 8:30 AM PST
👀 Follow @LorenHodl for the bat-signal.
🎧 Missed it live? Search Bitcoin Today Recast on your favorite podcast app.
Follow @BitcoinToday__ on X for the latest episodes.

Just another Monday in Bitcoin. Stay vigilant. ₿⚡

item.description:
Coinbase just launched fully backed tokenized stocks on Base. 

Dromos Labs’ Alex Cutler says they’ll chip away at Interactive Brokers "77% profit margin."

========================================================

Thank you to our sponsor!

  • ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Visit⁠⁠⁠⁠ 1inch.com⁠⁠⁠⁠ to swap tokenized securities, crypto and more. Simple. Secure. Self-custodial. Whatever asset you’re buying - swap it at⁠⁠⁠⁠ 1inch.com⁠⁠⁠⁠

========================================================

Coinbase this week launched tokenized versions of Apple, Nvidia, Meta, and Google stock on Base, moving past the prior synthetic tokenized-stock wrappers. The tokens are fully backed, held in trust, with ETF-style minting and redemption.

Alex Cutler, CEO and Co-Founder of Dromos Labs, joins Laura Shin to unpack what real backing changes about tokenized stocks, and to argue decentralized exchanges can beat legacy brokers on cost and access.

Cutler points to Aerodrome's roughly 25% share of AMM volume on the new assets, about $80 million traded and 5,000 wallets active within days, plus integrations across nine DeFi protocols including Aave, Morpho, and 1inch.

He argues Interactive Brokers extracts a 77% profit margin as a middleman, and cites Nvidia's earnings, released after the bell, as proof onchain markets kept pricing news around the clock.

They also cover the SEC innovation exemption and a roadmap of more assets, a Centrifuge migration to Aerodrome, and a launch on Circle's Arc chain.

item.title: The Bitcoin Infinity Show – How Bitcoin Podcasting Actually Works with Nick Malster | Bitcoin Infinity Show #218
item.description:
Nick Malster joins the Bitcoin Infinity Show to talk about building Fountain, the Bitcoin podcast app where listeners send sats over Lightning and creators publish to open RSS feeds instead of closed platforms. He explains why Fountain has wound down its listen to earn rewards, how AI generated podcast clones are flooding the apps and what the Podcast Index is doing about it, and where value for value monetization goes from here. Knut and Nick also get into copyright in the age of AI, an honest assessment of Nostr adoption, and why the old record deal model never worked for artists.

item.title: Bitcoin News Alerts | Daily BTC Macro Signal – 2442: $2 Million Bitcoin Accelerates - Why 99.6% of the World Still Owns Almost None
item.description:
Bitcoin ownership remains extraordinarily rare despite more than 17 years of adoption. An estimated 96.3% of humanity owns no Bitcoin, roughly 99.6% owns less than 0.01 BTC, and only around 825,000 people are estimated to own at least one whole Bitcoin. Episode 2342 examines what happens as you move further up the Bitcoin ownership distribution and why meaningful BTC ownership could become dramatically harder to achieve.

JV also breaks down the supply mathematics behind a potential $2 million Bitcoin price, including millions of BTC estimated to be permanently lost, Bitcoin's declining new issuance and competition from Wall Street, corporations, sovereign wealth funds and governments. As demand expands while Bitcoin's monetary policy remains fixed, higher prices become the mechanism required to convince existing holders to sell.

📺 Prefer video? Watch daily Bitcoin breakdowns: http://BitcoinNewsAlerts.net

]]>

item.title: House of Satoshi - Bitcoin und Friends – #64 Bitcoin, Gold und der US-Schuldenberg: Jeff Haindl redet Klartext
item.description:
Jeff Haindl hat letztes Jahr seine gesamten Bitcoin verkauft, obwohl er einen eigenen Bitcoin-Node zu Hause betreibt und sich seit Jahren tief mit der Technologie beschäftigt. Der Stuzz.ch-Mitgründer erklärt, warum ihn das Quantum-Computing-Risiko nervöser machte als jede Kurskorrektur, wie er heute wieder zukauft und weshalb Gold für ihn nach wie vor der verlässlichere Wertspeicher ist.


Zwischen 40 Billionen US-Schulden, Goldkäufen der Zentralbanken und der Frage, warum kaum ein Bitcoiner tatsächlich mit Bitcoin bezahlt, wird schnell klar: einfache Antworten gibt es hier keine.


Mehr zu Jeffery Haindl

Nach mehreren Jahren im Finanzbereich, u.a. lange Zeit im Hedgefonds-Business in New York, baut er heute mit Stuzz.ch Content, Weiterbildung und Beratung Richtung finanzieller Unabhängigkeit auf.


Worum geht's: Bitcoin, Gold, ein US-Schuldenberg von 40 Billionen Dollar und die Frage, was in dieser fragilen Finanzwelt eigentlich noch als Wertspeicher taugt.


  • Das unterschätzte Quantum-Risiko und Jeffs Komplettverkauf seiner Bitcoin, inklusive vorsichtigem Wiedereinstieg.
  • Bitcoin gegen Gold: Geschichte, Zentralbank-Akzeptanz und warum Gold für Jeff der festere Portfolio-Baustein bleibt.
  • Warum auch die Verwahrung von Bitcoin diversifiziert sein muss: Hardware-Wallet, Börse und ETF statt alles an einem Ort, eine Lehre, die auch aus dem Cold-Card-Sicherheitsvorfall stammt.
  • Portfolio-Aufteilung zwischen Aktien, Gold und Bitcoin, und warum Bitcoin für Jeff eine Einzelwette bleibt statt Basisinvestment.
  • Bitcoin als Zahlungsmittel in der Praxis: von Lugano über Prag bis zu einer Garküche in Bangkok.


Mehr Infos zu stuzz.ch: https://www.stuzz.ch/


📬 Unser Newsletter, Bitcoin und Krypto kompakt und verständlich, direkt für Schweizer Anleger: https://www.house-of-satoshi.ch/newsletter/

]]>

item.title: bitcoin ist - Wissen statt FOMO – 20) ... die Lösung für ein großes Problem
item.description:
Was passiert, wenn die Zentralbank immer wieder auf den Geldknopf drückt und die Geldmenge über einen langen Zeitraum immer weiter ansteigt? Heute sprechen wir über die offensichtlichen und weniger offensichtlichen Folgen der Inflation. Die Preise steigen an – klar, das weiss ja jeder. Aber sonst? Warum zum Beispiel haben wir langfristig weniger Geld zur Verfügung, wenn Hersteller auf minderwertige Qualität setzen?


In dieser Folge erfährst du:

  • wie Hersteller wegen gestiegener Kosten bei Rohstoffen zu ethisch fragwürdigen Praktiken verleitet werden und warum dich das langfristig Geld und Gesundheit kostet
  • was "Shrinkflation" bedeutet
  • wie Inflation mit steigender Obdachlosigkeit zusammenhängt
  • warum der Druck auf den Geldknopf zwar kurzfristig soziale Not lindern kann, dann aber langfristig wiederum in einem Teufelskreis enden muss, der noch mehr Leid erzeugt.


Bitcoin kommt heute mal wieder nur am Rande vor. Aber es ist notwendig, sich die Folgen der Inflation bildlich vors Auge zu führen. Ich war sehr betroffen, als ich das erste mal den Film "What's the Problem? von Joe Bryan gesehen habe. Selten bekommt man so eindrücklich aufgezeigt, wie Inflation unsere Gesellschaft Schicht für Schicht durchdringt und zersetzt. Ausdrückliche Empfehlung - bitte schaut es euch an!


Hier der Link:

- englische Originalversion

- deutsche Sprachfassung (Overdub)


Alles von "bitcoin ist..." Hier geht es zu allen meinen Kanälen

Einsteiger-Spezial: möchtest du wissen, WIE man bitcoin sicher kauft und verwahrt? Kostenlose und sichere Kaufanleitung direkt in dein Postfach

Hinterlasse mir gerne eine 5-Sterne-Bewertung oder einen Kommentar.

Danke, Dein Christian.

]]>

item.title: Thank God for Bitcoin – TGFB Podcast Episode 80: Angela McArdle: Faith, Freedom, and the Fight for Financial Privacy
item.description:
Angela McArdle shares her journey from a Christian missionary upbringing and a degree in organizational leadership at Biola University, through early work in litigation and community service — including volunteering on Skid Row with homeless veterans — to becoming chair of the LA County Libertarian Party after an unsuccessful but formative Congressional run. She reflects on how the COVID-19 debacle reshaped her friendships and values around community and shared principles, and discusses her current outreach to the Bitcoin community. Along the way, she makes the case that Christians can't afford to sit out politics, even though it's messy and corrupting, and explores how the anti-war movement is realigning across the political spectrum, with libertarianism emerging as common ground that unites people from otherwise opposing camps.

]]>

item.title: The Peter McCormack Show – #206 - Emad Mostaque - "Your Job's Economic Life Expectancy Ends In 2 Years"
item.description:
Emad Mostaque founded Stability AI, built Stable Diffusion, and helped kick off the open-source generative AI explosion - before stepping down to build a new blueprint for human freedom as founder and CEO of Intelligent Internet. A former hedge fund manager turned tech pioneer, he argues that we have reached the end of our "economic life expectancy," and that within two years, virtually any job that can be done remotely will be done cheaper, faster, and better by artificial intelligence.


Emad and I discuss why 50% of work tasks are about to collapse like a sand pile, the arrival of $1.50-an-hour humanoid robots that fit directly into human-shaped holes, and why the state will inevitably try to license AI and use brain-scanning technology to prevent you from lying.

item.title: Bitcoin Audible – Learning the Wrong Lessons
item.description:
Thousands of careful Bitcoiners just got wiped out by a Coldcard entropy bug, and I use this episode to push back hard on the idea that self-custody is dead, and "don't trust, verify" failed us.

I walk through the brutal history of centralized custodial failures, explain why "holding your own keys is still orders of magnitude safer, and extract three real lessons from this recent disaster. This is about keeping perspective, learning the right lessons from pain, and making Bitcoin self-custody stronger, not weaker.

item.title: Der Bitcoin Kompass: Wegweiser im Kaninchenbau – Folge 5: Der Bitcoin-Preis – Zwischen Angebot, Nachfrage und Geldpolitik
item.description:
Was bestimmt eigentlich den Bitcoin-Preis? In Folge 5 vom Bitcoin-Kompass sprechen wir üeber eines der meistdiskutierten Themen im Bitcoin-Space: den Preis. Dabei geht es nicht um Prognosen oder Kaufempfehlungen, sondern um ein grundlegendes Verständnis dafüer, wie der Bitcoin-Preis entsteht und welche Kraefte ihn beeinflussen.


Wir erklären, wie Angebot und Nachfrage auf Bitcoin-Börsen funktionieren, warum das Handelsvolumen oft wichtiger ist als der Preis selbst und welche Rolle die Marktkapitalisierung spielt. Ausserdem beleuchten wir die grossen Einflussfaktoren: das Bitcoin-Halving und den Vier-Jahres-Zyklus, die Geldpolitik der US-Notenbank (Fed), Inflation und die wachsenden Staatsschulden der USA. Im Vergleich zwischen Bitcoin und Gold zeigen sie, warum Bitcoin technologisch ueberlegen sein könnte - und warum der Preis letztlich ein Spiegel des wachsenden Vertrauens in diese neue Technologie ist.


Mehr Infos, interaktive Grafiken zur Marktkapitalisierung und Kontaktmoeglichkeiten findet ihr auf:


Webseite: https://derbitcoinkompass.ch

E-Mail: kontakt@derbitcoinkompass.ch

Telegram: https://t.me/btc_kaninchenbau


Feedback und Fragen gerne per E-Mail, ueber Telegram oder ueber unsere Webseite.



(00:00:00) Begruessung & Einfuehrung ins Thema Preis

(00:01:31) Volatilitaet und der aktuelle Bitcoin-Preis

(00:02:33) Kaufkraft, Inflation und warum Menschen investieren

(00:05:20) Marktkapitalisierung: Bitcoin vs. Gold vs. Immobilien vs. Aktien

(00:08:05) Wie entsteht der Bitcoin-Preis? Angebot & Nachfrage erklaert

(00:11:04) Warum das Handelsvolumen entscheidend ist

(00:12:43) Die grossen Einflussfaktoren auf den Bitcoin-Preis

(00:13:26) In was messen wir den Preis? Euro, Dollar oder Aepfel?

(00:17:03) Warum Geld kein stabiler Massstab ist

(00:18:10) Bitcoins festes Angebot: Maximal 21 Millionen

(00:20:02) Das Halving und der Vier-Jahres-Zyklus

(00:24:22) Die Fed, Zinspolitik und US-Staatsschulden

(00:31:27) Was bedeutet das alles fuer den Bitcoin-Preis?

(00:33:37) Bitcoin vs. Gold: Vorteile und Unterschiede

(00:40:30) Preisprognose: Bitcoin auf 1 Million Dollar?

(00:41:54) Zusammenfassung & Verabschiedung

]]>

item.title: Epicenter - Learn about Crypto, Blockchain, Ethereum, Bitcoin and Distributed Technologies – Why Crypto Finally Makes Sense to Wall Street | Jason Yanowitz
item.description:
Jason Yanowitz, Co-Founder of Blockworks, joins Sebastien Couture on Epicenter to discuss why crypto is entering its biggest transformation yet. From institutional adoption and the Clarity Act to token transparency, AI, on-chain capital markets and the acquisition of Messari, this conversation explores where crypto is actually heading.


Jason explains why Wall Street is preparing for crypto, why token fundamentals finally matter, how Blockworks acquired Messari, why capital markets are moving on-chain, and why the next crypto cycle could look completely different from previous bull markets.


The conversation also covers Bitcoin, Ethereum, DeFi, stablecoins, RWAs (Real World Assets), tokenisation, venture capital, crypto regulation, SEC policy, the Clarity Act, Token Transparency Framework, AI, Robinhood, Coinbase, Hyperliquid, self-custody, crypto infrastructure, institutional finance and the future of blockchain adoption.


In this episode:



1. Why Wall Street is preparing for crypto

2. The Blockworks × Messari acquisition

3. The Clarity Act and US crypto regulation

4. Token transparency and the future of crypto markets

5. Stablecoins, RWAs and on-chain capital markets

6. AI's role in the next generation of crypto businesses

7. Why the next crypto cycle will reward real fundamentals

8. Building one of crypto's leading media and data companies

item.title: VERIFIED by Bitcoin Suisse – Bitcoin's Worst Month Since the ETFs. Is the Bottom In?
item.description:
In this episode, our Head Research Dominic Weibel is joined by crypto protocol expert Wolfgang Vitale and newly-joined senior research associate Filippo Franchini for a dense companion to the bimonthly Industry Roll-Up. 

They unpack June's record $4.5B in US spot ETF outflows alongside a ~20% Bitcoin drawdown, why Strategy's dividend-funded sale of over 3,000 BTC triggered a relief rally rather than a real dump, and Hyperliquid's outlier month of positive flows. From there the conversation turns tactical: a bottom-indicator framework, a potential October cycle low, and a deep dive into Ethereum's roadmap toward what Vitalik Buterin is now calling Ethereum 3.0.

]]>

item.title: Krypto Corner – Bitcoin, ETF und NFT: Sicher investieren - Krypto verstehen und sicher starten – Kapitel 12: Ein Metronom für Mut: Der Krypto-Sparplan (DCA) ⏱️ | Krypto verstehen (Kapitel 12)
item.description:
Episode #12: Ein Metronom für Mut – Der DCA-Sparplan als emotionale Lebensversicherung

Wer täglich, stündlich oder gar minütlich auf die blinkenden Krypto-Charts starrt, verbrennt auf Dauer nicht nur sein hart verdientes Geld, sondern vor allem seine Lebensenergie und seine Nerven. In dieser wegweisenden Episode der Krypto Corner erklären Julian und Max unserer WG in Berlin das simple, aber extrem mächtige Prinzip von Dollar Cost Averaging (DCA).

Wir zeigen dir, wie du den Krypto-Markt mental besiegst, indem du nicht mehr versuchst, krampfhaft schlauer zu sein als er. Ein automatisierter Sparplan nimmt die Emotionen, die Gier und vor allem die Angst (FOMO) komplett aus dem Spiel. Anstatt dich über sinkende Kurse zu ärgern, lernst du durch diese simple Strategie, dich über "Rabatte" bei deinem nächsten automatischen Kauf im Bärenmarkt zu freuen.

Doch Vorsicht vor dem endlosen Papierkram! Im Steuer-Deep-Dive dieser Folge warnen wir eindringlich vor der enormen Datenflut, die ein bequemer DCA-Sparplan im Hintergrund erzeugt. Wir erklären den massiven Unterschied zwischen dem strengen FiFo-Prinzip (First-in, First-out) in Deutschland, das für jeden kleinsten Kauf eine eigene 1-Jahres-Frist startet, und der entspannten Methode des "gleitenden Durchschnitts" in Österreich. Zudem entlarven wir eine miese Gebührenfalle, die besonders Einsteiger mit kleinen monatlichen Sparraten heimlich in den Ruin treiben kann.

In dieser Folge erfährst du: • Warum der krampfhafte Versuch, den absoluten Tiefpunkt im Markt zu treffen ("Market Timing"), eine teure Illusion ist. • Wie ein automatisierter Sparplan Emotionen und Panik komplett aus deinem Anlageverhalten eliminiert. • Die mathematischen Vorteile des Durchschnittskosteneffekts im Bärenmarkt. • Wie das Finanzamt 52 Jahreskäufe in DE (FiFo-Tranchen) vs. AT (Gleitender Durchschnitt) steuerlich bewertet. • Warum pauschale Fixgebühren bei kleinen Krypto-Sparraten dein größter Feind sind und wie du sie umgehst.

Diese Episode basiert auf Kapitel 12 des Einsteiger-Romans „Krypto verstehen – sicher starten. Band 1“ von Sascha Swen Heiter. Verantwortung steht über Spekulation. Automatisiere deinen Einstieg, eliminiere die Emotionen und investiere mit Köpfchen!

📚 Das Buch zur Show: Wenn du das gesamte Wissen sofort anwenden möchtest – von der Einrichtung deiner Hardware Wallets über die Nutzung von Burner Wallets bis hin zu wichtigen rechtlichen und steuerlichen Themen in der DACH-Region – hol dir das komplette Buch! 👉 https://amzn.eu/d/06DuLLUw

🔗 FOLGE MIR FÜR MEHR KRYPTO-WISSEN: • Spotify:https://open.spotify.com/show/5MOMwCZpWNvm6J52jkdLcl?si=yq7YoMyZSnWCg_xrVLcnww • Apple Podcasts:https://podcasts.apple.com/de/podcast/krypto-corner-bitcoin-etf-und-nft-sicher-investieren/id1872914214 • Instagram:https://instagram.com/Swen_Heiter

👇 Unterstütze den Kanal: Wenn dir diese Folge geholfen hat, lass ein Abo da, gib dem Video einen Daumen nach oben und aktiviere die Glocke. Feedback oder Fragen zur Folge? Ab damit in die Kommentare!

⚖️ Rechtliche Hinweise / Haftungsausschluss: Die in diesem Podcast geteilten Inhalte dienen ausschließlich der allgemeinen Information sowie der Unterhaltung und stellen keine Anlage-, Rechts- oder Steuerberatung dar. Investitionen in Kryptowährungen sind hochriskant und können zu einem Totalverlust des eingesetzten Kapitals führen. Jeder Hörer und Zuschauer handelt absolut eigenverantwortlich. Besonders bei steuerlichen Themen ist zu beachten, dass die steuerliche Behandlung von Kryptowährungen sehr komplex ist. Bitte konsultiere für die aktuell geltende Rechtslage in der DACH-Region zwingend einen qualifizierten Steuerberater. Eine Haftung für Schäden, die aus der Nutzung der hier bereitgestellten Informationen entstehen, wird ausdrücklich ausgeschlossen.

#KryptoCorner #DCASparplan #KryptoSparplan #BitcoinDCA #KryptoSteuern #FiFo #KryptoVerstehen #SaschaSwenHeiter #KryptoAnfänger #Podcast #Kapitel12


]]>

In dieser Folge erfährst du: • Warum der krampfhafte Versuch, den absoluten Tiefpunkt im Markt zu treffen ("Market Timing"), eine teure Illusion ist. • Wie ein automatisierter Sparplan Emotionen und Panik komplett aus deinem Anlageverhalten eliminiert. • Die mathematischen Vorteile des Durchschnittskosteneffekts im Bärenmarkt. • Wie das Finanzamt 52 Jahreskäufe in DE (FiFo-Tranchen) vs. AT (Gleitender Durchschnitt) steuerlich bewertet. • Warum pauschale Fixgebühren bei kleinen Krypto-Sparraten dein größter Feind sind und wie du sie umgehst.

Diese Episode basiert auf Kapitel 12 des Einsteiger-Romans „Krypto verstehen – sicher starten. Band 1“ von Sascha Swen Heiter. Verantwortung steht über Spekulation. Automatisiere deinen Einstieg, eliminiere die Emotionen und investiere mit Köpfchen!

item.description:
Folge #61 – Ein Gespräch über Banken IT und Bitcoin Bücher

Harald Beetz ist seit fast 20 Jahren selbstständig in der Beratung für Banken und Rechenzentren. Angefangen als Banklehrling bei der Sparkasse, hat er früh den Wandel von Beratung hin zu reinem Vertrieb erlebt und sich auf IT-Projekte spezialisiert. In diesem Gespräch erzählt er, wie er von der Banken IT zu Bitcoin kam, warum er mit seiner Frau einen Roman über Geld schrieb und wie er sich heute zwischen Beratung und Content rund um Bitcoin positioniert.


Du erfährst,

  • wie Harald die Bankenwelt von innen erlebt hat,
  • welche Herausforderungen und Chancen es als IT-Berater gibt,
  • warum er Bitcoin zunächst wieder verkaufte und später mit völlig anderem Blick neu entdeckte,
  • wie aus einer Buchidee seiner Frau ein gemeinsames Projekt wurde
  • und welche unternehmerischen Lektionen er aus fast zwei Jahrzehnten Selbstständigkeit mitnimmt.

item.title: Should I Invest in Bitcoin? Grow Your Wealth & Understand the Cryptocurrency Bit Coin, for Millennials Serious About Money and Investing – What Actually Caused Bitcoin's Biggest Week in History (23%) and Why September Could Ruin It (Bit Coin, Wealth & Investing)
item.description:
Bitcoin added over $14,000 in seven days. That is the largest dollar gain of any week in its history. Not 2017. Not 2021. Ever.

And it happened immediately after Fidelity reported that Bitcoin had been quieter than it had been on 98.5% of days in its entire existence. The market was not dead in July. It was compressed.

In this episode you will discover:

  • Why this was the biggest week ever in dollars but only the second best since 2021 in percentage terms, and what that tells you about how much Bitcoin has grown up
  • What the US Treasury bond buyback programme actually is, explained properly and simply, and why a government borrowing money to buy back money it already borrowed is the real story underneath this rally
  • Why the people who quietly stopped stacking in July are now about to make the single most expensive mistake in investing, and why September is historically Bitcoin's worst month of the year

I built a free calculator that shows exactly what consistent monthly Bitcoin investing could do to your wealth over 5, 10 or 20 years. It's called the Steady Stack Calculator — punch in what you can afford to put in each month and see what the numbers actually look like at the other end. Most people are genuinely surprised. You can also download the 10 Bitcoin Mistakes to Avoid document completely free at the same link.

Steady Stack Calculator and 10 Bitcoin Mistakes Document — click here to grab both for free

Hit follow, so you never miss the latest insights on money, finance, invest and build wealth - plus clear guidance on cryptocurrency, Bitcoin, and Bit Coin for today’s serious investors.

item.title: BTC-ECHO Recap | Top-Stories zu Bitcoin & Kryptowährungen – Wir sind umgezogen!
21talk – Sie verfolgen deine Bitcoin! So schützt du deine Privatsphäre I 21talk mit Timo Volkov
item.description:
In dieser Folge von 21talk begrüßt Dino Heinert (21bitcoin) den Privacy-Experten und Autor Timo Volkov, um über eines der wichtigsten Themen im digitalen Zeitalter zu sprechen: den Schutz der eigenen Privatsphäre. Timo, der Verfasser des „Privacy Handbuch“, teilt wertvolle Einblicke darüber, wie man die Balance zwischen digitaler Bequemlichkeit und notwendiger Diskretion findet und warum Privatsphäre gerade für Bitcoin-Nutzer ein unverzichtbares Gut ist.Das Gespräch bietet praktische Lösungen für den Alltag, von Browser-Empfehlungen und sicheren Handy-Setups wie GrapheneOS bis hin zu tiefgehenden Analysen über die Anonymität von Bitcoin On-Chain und im Lightning-Netzwerk. Gemeinsam räumen die beiden mit gängigen Mythen auf und zeigen auf, wie jeder mit einfachen „Quick Wins“ seine digitalen Spuren minimieren und die Kontrolle über seine persönlichen Daten zurückgewinnen kann.Das Privacy Handbuch - Timo Volkov: https://privatopia.de/das-privacy-handbuch/

(00:00) Intro(00:39) Das Privacy-Handbuch(00:59) Browser-Empfehlungen: Brave Browser für Handy & Desktop(02:00) Timos Weg zu Privacy: Bitcoin als Einstieg(04:47) Wer braucht mehr Privatsphäre?(07:58) Aufwand vs. Nutzen: Die Privacy-Skala(10:22) Drei Quick Wins für mehr Privatsphäre(12:28) VPN-Empfehlungen(14:45) GrapheneOS und Pixel-Handys(16:48) Mythen: Wie privat ist Apple wirklich?(18:10) Computer-Setup & Hardware-Tipps(20:06) Kosten und Zeitaufwand für Privacy(22:52) Bitcoin & Privatsphäre: On-Chain vs. Layer 2 (Lightning/Liquid)(26:26) Workshops & kritischer Blick auf CoinJoins(29:02) Privatsphäre in der Finanzwelt: Bargeld & Gutscheine(30:33) Einfluss von KI auf die Privatsphäre(33:46) Trend: Warum Privatsphäre immer wichtiger wird(36:18) Social Media & bewusste Entscheidungen

item.title: Bitcoin Rails | Isabel Foxen Duke – Bitcoin's Leading Post-Quantum Signature Proposal | CONDUITION
item.description:
The first fully specified post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin has been proposed to the Bitcoin mailing list.

The proposal introduces a full specification for “SHRINCS,” a hash-based signature scheme initially conceived by Jonas Nick and Mikhail Kudinov of Blockstream Research — with specification details added by new co-authors Conduition, Remix7531 and BIP 360 co-author Ethan Heilman.

Today, I’m honored to share a full whiteboard explanation of the scheme by its co-author Conduition, as well as thorough discussion of the scheme’s key tradeoffs when compared to Bitcoin’s existing elliptic-curve signatures and competing post-quantum alternatives.

In more detail, this interview includes:

— A full whiteboard walkthrough of the scheme’s key components and its relationship to the NIST-standardized scheme SPHINCS+

— SHRINCs’ introduction of a compact stateful path - yes, I said stateful 🌶️

— Whiteboard explanations of all relevant cryptographic subschemes, including FORS, WOTS+C, and XMSS

— Thorough discussion of the scheme’s tradeoffs and implications for Bitcoin’s existing functionality

If you have a vested interest in understanding what may be the future signature scheme protecting Bitcoin transactions in a post-quantum world, this episode is a must-watch.

WARNING: this episode is fairly technical — don't beat yourself up if you don't catch everything, or need to watch it a few times to grok the details.

This episode of Bitcoin Rails is brought to you by:

LayerTwo Labs @LayerTwoLabs — developing research, software, and technologies for scaling Bitcoin via the integration of Drivechains (BIP 300/301)

Hashi on @SuiNetwork — a primitive for executing Bitcoin DeFi transactions, without having to trust a federated bridge or other centralized entity

BitBox @BitBoxSwiss — an open-source Bitcoin-only hardware wallet, with smooth UX and no compromises on security. Check out Bitbox [dot] swiss and use code BITCOINRAILS to get a discount

]]>

item.title: Bitcoin Bundesverband Podcast – #2 Vorstandsvorstellung
item.description:
Am 26. September 2024 wurde der ⁠Bitcoin Bundesverband⁠ offiziell gegründet, und der erste Vorstand wurde gewählt. Zum Vorstandsvorsitzenden wurde Philipp Hartmannsgruber ernannt, sein Stellvertreter ist Daniel Wingen, und Matthias Steger übernimmt das Amt des Finanzvorstands. Weitere Vorstandsmitglieder sind Evelyn Brock, Jens Leinert, Dr. Mathias Linkerhand und Lars Eichhorst. In dieser Folge stellt sich das Team vor.

item.title: HashrateUp - A Bitcoin Mining Podcast – They Could Have Built This Years Ago. Nobody Did.
item.description:
Michael Schmidt, better known as Schnitzel, bought a hundred S19J Pros for $40 each. Machines that used to cost $15,000. He's bringing them back with open-source firmware he built in his garage, with help from an AI agent and about eight burned hashboards along the way.


Michael is one of the lead engineers at the 256 Foundation, and he's back on the show to talk about Magina. It's an open-source firmware that does things Braiins, Luxor, Vnish and stock firmware simply won't. You can ramp a miner from 3,000W down to 1,000W in three to five seconds, where other firmware takes half an hour. You can follow a live solar curve. And you can run hashboards from completely different machines together in one rig, which no proprietary firmware will let you do.


We talk about why nobody built any of this before, why the 256 Foundation wants open rigs but not open chips, and what happened when Michael handed an AI agent an S19 and a power meter and told it to figure things out. We also get into why your miner's power API is lying to you about wattage, what he learned from destructive testing across eight different hashboard variants, and where he thinks this all goes over the next two or three years.


👤 Guest: Michael Schmidt (Schnitzel), Lead Engineer at the 256 Foundation

256 Foundation: https://www.256foundation.org

Follow on X: https://x.com/schnitzel


Timestamps:


0:00 Intro: Schnitzel, Teddy the Swiss mountain dog & proof of dog

3:04 The 256 Foundation: Libreboard, Ember One, Magina & Hydro Pool

4:13 Heat reuse goes commercial: the Swiss solar monetization project

5:00 The solar problem: chasing a production curve that never sits still

5:31 Why existing firmware takes 30 minutes to change wattage

6:35 Why nobody built sub-minute ramping before (and why it isn't malicious)

9:18 Proprietary hardware: the tire manufacturer who only sells whole cars

10:57 Open rigs, not open chips: what the 256 Foundation actually wants

13:52 What Magina is and how it differs from Braiins, Luxor & Vnish

15:06 Handing an AI agent an S19 and a Shelly power meter

17:03 Zero to 500 MHz: the board that died and the ramping fix

19:21 Destructive testing: 8 hashboard variants in a single S19J Pro

20:22 Physical vs digital: 2,900W on the API, 0W on the wall

22:10 Microphones, temp sensors and eight burned boards

24:13 Why the power API guesses, and why the PSU already knows

27:09 S19J + S19K on one control board: 130 TH/s from mismatched hardware

31:30 Building a Frankenstein miner from two dead machines

32:25 The $40 miner renaissance and bringing dead hardware back

34:04 Magina on a Canaan Nano, Proto chips and the wildfire moment

35:08 Get involved: dev calls, donations and hardware you're not using


🛠 Sponsored by:


Luxor. Mining pool, firmware, hardware trading & hashrate tools

https://luxor.tech/


Altair Technology. ASIC hardware, replacement parts & mining infrastructure

Code: HASHRATEUP

https://altairtech.io/aff/125/


📊 HashrateUp Hardware Deals: https://t.me/hashrateup

📩 Free 5-Day Bitcoin Mining Course: https://hashrateup.com/newsletter-sign-up/


#BitcoinMining #OpenSource #Magina #256Foundation #Heatpunk #HeatReuse #SolarMining #ASIC #S19 #Firmware #AI #BitcoinMiningFirmware #Bitcoin #HashrateUp

item.title: Bitcoin Policy Institute – Spotlight Series Ep. 2: Rep. Nick Begich
item.description:
Rep. Nick Begich (R-AK) reached Congress by an unusual route: founding software companies and holding Bitcoin since 2013. BPI's David Zell sat down with him at PubKey to talk about how a builder's instincts shape the way he legislates, his bill to give the U.S. a strategic Bitcoin reserve, and the policy questions AI is raising faster than Washington can answer them.


The conversation runs from Begich's 440 coins on Mt. Gox, to the American Reserve Modernization Act (ARMA), the ~93-year cycle of global reserve currencies, the "untethering" of money from scarcity, and why he believes AI's hardest problem is the "disintermediation of purpose" rather than unemployment. They close on UBI, Alaska's Permanent Fund as a model of citizen ownership, and what's next for the budget and healthcare.


Guest: Rep. Nick Begich (R-AK)

Host: David Zell, Bitcoin Policy Institute

Recorded at PubKey


CHAPTERS

0:00 Intro: A Founder Comes to Congress

1:21 From Baylor to Ford to Building a Software Company

5:17 Finding Bitcoin in 2013 & Surviving Mt. Gox

6:44 The Founder's Mindset vs. the Zero-Sum Worldview

13:56 ARMA: The Case for a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve

19:25 The "Untethering Event": Scarcity, Inflation & the Debt Spiral

25:58 AI's Promise, Peril & the "Disintermediation of Purpose"

31:59 Open-Source AI, China & Catastrophic Misuse Risk

39:14 Drawing the Regulatory Line & the "Bitcoin of AI"

42:25 UBI vs. Alaska's Permanent Fund: "Universal Basic Investment"

49:43 What's Next: The Budget, Healthcare & Quantum


#Bitcoin #BitcoinPolicy #ARMA #NickBegich #AIPolicy #DigitalAssets #StrategicBitcoinReserve #BPI #Crypto #MonetaryPolicy

]]>

BPI's David Zell sat down with him at PubKey to talk about how a builder's instincts shape the way he legislates, his bill to give the U.S. a strategic Bitcoin reserve, and the policy questions AI is raising faster than Washington can answer them.


The conversation runs from Begich's 440 coins on Mt. Gox, to the American Reserve Modernization Act (ARMA), the ~93-year cycle of global reserve currencies, the "untethering" of money from scarcity, and why he believes AI's hardest problem is the "disintermediation of purpose" rather than unemployment. They close on UBI, Alaska's Permanent Fund as a model of citizen ownership, and what's next for the budget and healthcare.


Guest: Rep. Nick Begich (R-AK)

Host: David Zell, Bitcoin Policy Institute

Recorded at PubKey


CHAPTERS

0:00 Intro: A Founder Comes to Congress

1:21 From Baylor to Ford to Building a Software Company

5:17 Finding Bitcoin in 2013 & Surviving Mt. Gox

6:44 The Founder's Mindset vs. the Zero-Sum Worldview

13:56 ARMA: The Case for a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve

19:25 The "Untethering Event": Scarcity, Inflation & the Debt Spiral

25:58 AI's Promise, Peril & the "Disintermediation of Purpose"

31:59 Open-Source AI, China & Catastrophic Misuse Risk

39:14 Drawing the Regulatory Line & the "Bitcoin of AI"

42:25 UBI vs. Alaska's Permanent Fund: "Universal Basic Investment"

49:43 What's Next: The Budget, Healthcare & Quantum


#Bitcoin #BitcoinPolicy #ARMA #NickBegich #AIPolicy #DigitalAssets #StrategicBitcoinReserve #BPI #Crypto #MonetaryPolicy

item.title: The Bitcoin Treasury Podcast – $4 Billion Asset Manager Reveals The Bitcoin Argument Wall Street Can No Longer Make
item.description:
Matt Tuttle is CEO of Tuttle Capital Management, an ETF issuer running roughly four to five billion dollars across thematic, options-based and event-driven funds. He has been on Wall Street since 1990 and came to Bitcoin through the ETF wrapper rather than through conviction. His argument is that the wrapper was the entire event: once BlackRock launched IBIT the skeptic case stopped being arguable, and his client portfolios now carry 6.25% Bitcoin against an industry standard of one to two percent.

item.title: Coin Stories with Natalie Brunell – Is the AI Buildout the Next Debt Crisis Trigger?
item.description:
AI is the latest technology that will change the world. That doesn't mean every dollar poured into building it will pay off.

Nearly $3 trillion is expected to be spent on data centers between 2025 and 2028, and roughly half of it is borrowed -- financed on the assumption that demand keeps exploding.

In this explainer episode:

  • What's actually inside a data center
  • Why they cost billions to build
  • Who's lending the money, and what they were promised in return
  • Why this boom has pulled capital away from Bitcoin
  • The one thing that has to keep happening, or the whole thing breaks

I also share why this matters for markets, your retirement account, and ultimately Bitcoin.

item.title: Nerd Culture • A Gamekings Podcast – #273 over Lanterns, Robocop & Avengers: Endgame Encore
item.description:
Nerd Culture #273 is ook te bekijken op https://youtu.be/o1A1XEaojwA 

Ook deze week word je weer bijgebracht met het allerlaatste nerdnieuws in aflevering 273 van Nerd Culture! Daarbij is Jelle weer aangeschoven aan de desk, en die heeft niet (of misschien juist wel) stilgezeten! Samen met Huey gaan zij door de hele waslijst met een uitgebreide bespreking van Lanterns, en in het verlengde daarvan ook The Green Lantern met Ryan Reynolds. Ook de oude vedetten van de show komen aan bod, met X-Men '97, Ted Lasso, Strange New Worlds, maar ook met een klein randje aan krulsnordraaiende arthouse ÉN een klein segmentje comics.

Een eerbetoon, een brief & het bespreken van arthouse tot frikandellen-TV

Het tweetal ontkomt er natuurlijk ook niet aan om even stil te staan bij alle artiesten die ons deze week zijn ontnomen en hun nalatenschap. Maar gelukkig wordt de sfeer (deels) opgevrolijkt door een kijkersvraag met een kritische blik op vormgeving, en is het al helemaal lachen, gieren, brullen tijdens de nieuwe trailer van Ali G: Who Iz I? Toch brengt dit bij Huey ook wel de vraag naar boven of hij niet inmiddels te oud is geworden voor die humor. Een ding waar ze niet te oud voor zijn geworden, is de Akira 4K re-release die binnenkort weer uitkomt en waar ze toch wel oren naar hebben.

Avengers: Endgame Encore & heeft Jelle ook zo'n zin in Doomsday?

Een groot punt dat aangehaald moest worden, en al zeker met onze huisfilmmaker Jelle in the building, is de re-release van Avengers: Endgame 'Encore'. Aan de herinnering overgelaten leek de film al prachtig, maar hij moest blijkbaar een heruitgave krijgen met de nodige kleurcorrectie. Is dit een pontificale promotie voor Avengers: Doomsday, of was het ook echt nodig? Of dat een Mandela-effect is gebleken, het enthousiasme van Huey en Jelle voor Doomsday op gelijke hoogte ligt, en nog veel meer van het laatste film- en superheldennieuws krijg je te horen in deze aflevering van Nerd Culture!

Wil je adverteren bij de podcast Nerd Culture óf misschien bij een andere podcast van ILVY Network? Mail dan naar management@ilvy.com en/of kijk even op de website: https://ilvy.com/podcast

See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.

]]>

Of dat een Mandela-effect is gebleken, het enthousiasme van Huey en Jelle voor Doomsday op gelijke hoogte ligt, en nog veel meer van het laatste film- en superheldennieuws krijg je te horen in deze aflevering van Nerd Culture!
